title: Critical Areas
description: A critical care (or ICU) nurse provides life-saving, specialized care for patients with severe, unstable, or life-threatening conditions . They work in high-stress environments like intensive care units (ICUs) to constantly monitor vital signs, operate life-support equipment, administer potent medications, and rapidly respond to medical emergencies. [ 1 , 2 ] Core Responsibilities Continuous Patient Monitoring: Tracking cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological functions while interpreting complex medical data and trends. [ 1 , 2 ] Life-Support Management: Operating and troubleshooting intricate machines, including mechanical ventilators, cardiac monitors, and intravenous (IV) pumps. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] Medication Administration: Calculating and titrating specialized IV medications (like vasoactive drugs) based on the patient's immediate clinical response. [ 1 , 2 ] Bedside Procedures: Assisting doctors with intubations, inserting arterial or central lines, changing dressings, and managing catheters. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] Patient & Family Support Advocacy: Acting as the primary voice for heavily sedated or incapacitated patients. Family Communication: Translating complex medical terminology into clear updates for distressed family members and helping them navigate the ICU environment. [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 ] Collaboration Interdisciplinary Teams: Working closely with physicians, respiratory therapists, pharmacists, and specialists to evaluate needs and refine the patient's care plan. [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] Because of the high-acuity nature of the unit, ICU nurses typically care for only 1 or 2 patients at a time. This low ratio allows them to maintain a hyper-vigilant eye on subtle changes in a patient's condition to prevent medical emergencies before they happen. [ 1 ] Where They Work While typically associated with general Intensive Care Units, critical care nurses also practice in highly specific departments, including: [ 1 , 2 ] Neonatal and Pediatric ICUs (NICU/PICU) Trauma and Burn Centers Cardiovascular Intensive Care Units (CICU) Emergency Departments and Mobile Medical Transport [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]
